div.head: Again the book of Shafte (Judges), that is s far daiyane (Book of Judges). Chapters, 16.

div.ab: First a proem. The name of Shafte (Judges) or Daiyane (Judges), in Hebrew is pronounced Shafatim, for it is not Shavte with Beth which means families. According to some, Finhas, the father of Eli the priest, who descended from Finhas the son of Eliazar, wrote this book; and according to others, Samuel the prophet.

div.head: Chapter I.
div.ab:
Chapter I. 1:2 And the Lord said Judah shall go up i.e., This is for the glory of the tribe from which the Messiah is promised. 1:2 Behold I have delivered the land into his hand i.e., in a spiritual (sense) in the hands of our Lord. 1:3 And Judah said unto Simon his brother come up with me in my lot with Pethaha of Sadhe. 1:6 And they caught him and cut his great thumbs and great toes i.e., (1:5)the lord of Bazaq as he himself did to 70 kings who used to gather up the bread from under his table. (cf. 1:7) God repaid him. Of old the chiefs of villages at that time were called kings. 1:12 I shall give him akhsa my daughter as a wife. i.e., Also in the book of Joshua the son of Nun, the story is mentioned. 1:14 And she dismounted from the donkey Gr. and she murmured from off the donkey and cried out In the land of the south you gave me i.e., where they were in short of water. 1:16 And the sons of Qinai, Moses'
father-in-law. i.e., he was called Qinai because of the abundance of his possessions; and because in the law it was not said that Huvar went up with those of the house of Israel when Moses asked that he go up, here he shows that he went up. 1:16 They went up from the city of the palm-trees i.e., from Jericho. 1:16 which is on the south of adhar. 1:17 Those inhabiting Sufath and they devoted it to utter destruction. i.e., they made a vow in regard to it. 1:27 to Beth-Sha an and to Ta nakh....and to the inhabitants of Dur. 1:29 he who dwelt in Gazar. 1:30 to the inhabitants of Qitrun and Yahlil. 1:31 And Ashir did not destroy the inhabitants of Akka and Saidun, nor of Hevel, nor of Izavel, and nor of Hallana, and nor to Afaq, and nor to Rahuv. 1:35 And the Amorites were persuaded to dwell in the land of Hadhes in the mountain Gr. where the bears and the foxes are. 2:1 And the angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Bikhyan. i.e., from the point where the Lord began to distribute (Lit., make to inherit) abundances unto them. He started (Lit., rises up) and reproached them for they trespassed the word of God and did not destroy the heathen nations.

div.head: Chapter II.
div.ab:
Chapter II. 2:11 And the children of Israel did evil before the Lord and served Ba la. i.e., Ba la is an image of Nava (Nebo) who is Hermes, who is set up beside the image of Istra (Ishtar) which is Peradhiti (Aphrodite) as a husband standing beside a wife; for their spheres in the sky are near each other
(namely the two planets, Mercury and Venus). And Istrathe (Ishtars) are many images which are fashioned after a female being. 3:1 And these are the nations which the Lord had left to prove through them the sons of Israel. i.e., when they provoke his anger he would give them power over them, (as) for example the five princes of the Philistines. 3:3 And all the Canaanites and the Sidonians and the Hivites that (were) in the mountain of Lebanon. 3:8 And he delivered them unto the hands of Kushan, the wicked king of Aram Nahrin (Mesopotamia). 3:15 And the Lord raised for them a savior Ahur, the son of Gara with Pethaha of Gamal, Nestorian with Revasa 3:15 a man whose right hand was crippled. Gr., an ambidextrous man, i.e., left-handed man who uses his left hand as his right hand. 3:16 And Ahur made for himself a sword of two edges Gr., a dagger that had two edges. 3:16 a span in length with Pethaha of Pe, Nest. with Revasa. Gr., Its length (was) a span. 3:17 And king Eglon was a very fat man. Gr., a very charming (refined) man. 3:19 I have a word in secret which I say to you, (O!) king. with vowelless Tau and fricative. Gr., a hidden (secret) word I have with you (O!) king.

div.head: Chapter III.
div.ab:
Chapter III. 3:20 And he was sitting in an upper chamber alone which he constructed for himself. with Pethaha of Mim. Gr., In a summer upper chamber. 3:22 And his belly came out after his blow with a vowelless first Qaf, and with Revasa of the
latter. (
) Gr., and he thrusted the haft also after the blade; i.e., after the sharp edge of the dagger. 3:22 and the fat closed the wound because he did not draw out the sword from his belly. i.e., the sword. 3:23 And Ahur went out to the porch i.e., to the upper chamber. Gr., to the Perustadha (Greek word meaning porch). 3:24 And they saw the doors of the upper chamber closed. i.e., kept shut. 3:24 and they said perhaps he went forth to the private chamber with Qushshaya of Tau and dalath. i.e., place of honor. 3:26 And as they were dismayed Gr., were afraid 3:26 Ahur crossed to the stone-quarries Gr. engraved images 3:26 and escaped and ran to Shirath. 3:31 Shamgar the son of enath, and he smote from the Philistines 600 men with an ox-goad Gr., besides the bull-calves. Ad., with the shaft(Lit., the knee) of the plough. 4:2 And the captain of his host (was) Sisera 4:2 in Harshath 4:4 And Deborah the prophetess, the wife of Pithar, was judging Israel in that time. i.e., it seemed she was a widow at that time. 4:6 And she sent, she called Baraq the son of Ahin em. 4:11 And Havar Qinai went out (separated himself) from Qin from the children of Havar i.e., Havar is Havav the son of Re a el who was Yathrun the father-in-law of Moses. 4:18 And ana el i.e., the wife of Havar, 4:18 went out to meet Sisera
4:18 And she covered him with wrap (quilt).i.e., a blanket rug. Gr., a curtain of her own. 4:19 Give me some water to drink, for I am thirsty; and she opened a skin of milk and gave him to drink. Gr., a jar of milk. 4:21 And she struck the peg into his temple. 4:21 when he was asleep with Revasa of Mim. 4:21 and he agonized and died. Gr., and he writhed in agony between her feet and died.

div.head: Chapter IV.
div.ab:
Chapter IV. The Song of praise of Deborah. 5:3 Hear, Oh ye kings, and listen, Oh ye princes Gr., Listen O! ye satraps (governors). 5:3 And I sing to the Lord with Pethaha of Zain. 5:4 Also the heavens dripped and the clouds dropped water. 5:3 And the mountains disappeared before the Lord. Gr., quivered. 5:7 They cut down the open spaces of Israel. i.e., The enemies destroyed villages that had no walls. 5:8 He chooses a new god, then barley bread. i.e., God chose a woman to rise up at the head of a great nation and prophesy, a new thing which is not customary. And thus he is to choose Gideon, who is called a round loaf of barley bread in the dream. Gr., They loved vain gods as (they liked?) barley bread. i.e., whose flavor is not delicious, and whose nourishment is scant. 5:9 Saying to the law-giver of Israel i.e., to God or the high-priest. 5:9 Those distinguished among the nation i.e., the scribes and the sages, and the chiefs. 5:10 And the riders of white donkeys i.e., as that for pleasure in the streets.
5:11 Then the people of the Lord came down to the door. i.e., of the tabernacle. Gr., They went down to their cities. i.e., those that fled. 5:12 Awake, awake, Deborah awake, and be strengthened i.e., she was loved by the people with words of praise. 5:12 Rise up Baraq and lead away your captives. 5:13 Then came down the deliverer i.e., Baraq. 5:13 who came down to me with a man (Lit., in a man) from Ephraim. 5:14 And his servants are in Amliq i.e., she filled the place of Joshua, the son of Nun, the Ephraimite, and did as Moses (did) unto Amliq. 5:14 After thee Benjamin, in thy love i.e., Saul who was about to destroy the reaminder of Amliq. 5:14 from Makhir came out a law-giver i.e., Gideon (
) the teacher of war or Niftah 5:14 and from Zevalan those that write with the reed of the scribe. i.e., in this tribe scribes were many. 5:15 He is sent on his foot (in his feet) to the division of Ruvil i.e., to show the humiliation of Baraq 5:15 many are the searchers of heart. i.e., Moses, Aaron, and Joshua. 5:16 Why sit you among the ways (paths) to hear the breathing (snorting) of the wild-ass i.e., reproaching the sons of Ruvil, who sit to listen to rumors and would not go to battle. 15:17 And Dan why did he drag ships Gr., and why did Dan dwell in
ships. 5:17 Ashir dwelt on the coast of the sea, and in its clefts he camped. 5:18 Zevalon was a people that reproached itself unto death. i.e., until death he was contending for his land and his people. In Greek there is placed after Zevalon a verse-ending. 5:19 possession and silver did not (they) take. i.e., the enemies, from that which belongs to us. 5:20 from their places the stars waged war, a battle from heaven with Sisera in the valley of Qishan. i.e., The saed of Ibrahim which the Lord likened unto the stars. With a power from heaven he fought and was victorious. 5:23 Curse Marudh i.e., The city which did not help Israel. 5:26 And her right hand upon the hammer of the carpenter. Gr., upon the chisels of the carvers. 5:26 And she smote Sisera and broke his head. with Pethaha of Pe and Rukkakha of Tau and Kof. Gr. She shattered his head and was crushing it. 5:27 And between her feet he knelt down, fell, and lay. with pethaha of Resh. 5:28 And from the window she looked out i.e., the prophetess was mocking the Gentile. 5:28 and the mother of Sisera wailed (Lit. shouted) from the balcony, and said. Gr., was looking and watching thru the lattice. i.e., a lattice-work or railing which is the balustrade, and in one codex ( ) a forged brass which is placed before the door of the chancel, just outside the wooden door. 5:28 wherefore i.e., because of what delays the noise (tumult) of his chariots? i.e., the noise of iron and brass. 5:28 of his chariots 5:31 And your beloved
ones are like the going out of the sun in his might. i.e., his strength.

div.head: Chapter V.
Chapter VI.
div.ab:
Chapter VI. 7:5 And the Lord said to Gideon, every one who laps the water with his tongue as the dog laps, set them (group) together. i.e., with these 300 who thru their weakness neglected to kneel down and drink, but moistened their tongues with their hands, God saved them. For by (Lit., in) weak persons God often shows his power. And according to some, because of their earnestness they did not tarry to drink but in haste they lapped and crossed; and according to others, each had a single hand, and because of that they were unable to lap. And according to our own idea, there is represented by them the type of the saints, who, of things desired make use only of the necessities. 7:5 And every one that kneels on his knees to drink, set him alone. i.e., the type of those that are attached to bodily desires and are not of (any) use. 7:10 Go down you and Pira your boy servant unto the camp. 7:13 And Gideon came and saw a man narrating a dream to his friend, and he said to him I saw a round loaf of barley-bread with Qushshaya of the two Kof. Aq. an ash-cake. Sim. -- a cake of bread. Turning over Gr., rolling. In the camp of Midian, and it reached the tent-camp, i.e., of Midian and overthrew it upside-down with Rukkakka of Pe and Qushshaya of Kof. And the tent
fell. 7:14 His friend answered and said to him, this is nothing but the sword of Gideon. i.e., It is the type of voluntary poverty and frugality in food overcoming all passionate desires. 7:16 And empty cruses and torches inside the cruses. i.e., in the pots and small jars they hid the light of the torches until they entered the camp of the enemies suddenly and surprised them. 7:18 And they said a sword to the Lord and to Gideon. i.e., to the Lord as well as to the maker, and to Gideon as to the organ (instrument). 7:22 Until Beth-Shavte and until Sadhdath. 7:22 of Avel Mehula which is next (Lit., over) Yatbath. 7:25 And they killed uziv in Sur and Ziv he killed in Beth Qavrav. 8:2 Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Izer el? An interrogation. i.e., you came during the latter part of the war, and yet destroyed the chieftains. 8:4 Running and fainting Gr., hungry. 8:6 Is the hand of Zavah and Salmena in your hands now so that we give bread to your host? i.e., as reproaching Gideon, the chiefs of Sakkuth were saying these (things). 8:7 I will tread upon your flesh on thorns. Gr., I shall comb (card - cf. Alex. text).

div.head: Chapter VII.
Chapter VIII.
div.ab:
Chapter VIII. 9:26 And Ga al the son of afar. 9:27 And they made a banquet Gr., Dance. Heb. dances. 9:28 And Zaval who mediated (Lit., changed) his command served the people of Hamur, the father of Shekim, why should we serve
him ourselves? i.e., Ga al son of Afar scorned Zaval the governor of Shekim, for he had permitted himself to be enslaved to Abi-malik. And also Gr., Very clear is this word which he says And Zaval was an overseer (Episkopos) Also a servant with the men of Hamur the father of Shekim, to Abi-malik; and what is it that we should serve a servitude we 9:36 And Zaval said to him, it is the shadow of the mountain you see as men. i.e., mocking agal who a little while before was threatening Abi-malik, but at this moment, in fear, says thus. 9:37 Behold a nation coming down from the center of the land with a vowelless Qof. Gr., from the side of the navel of the land. 9:37 And one division is coming on the way of Beth-Balluta of Me unin Gr., of the seers. 9:41 And Abi-Malik dwelt in Adhama 9:45 And he destroyed the village and sowed it sea-purslane. with pethaha of Mim. i.e., 9:46 The princes of the tower 9:48 To the mountain of Salmun 9:50 And he encamped in Tavas 9:53 And a woman threw down a piece of the upper mill-stone on the head of Abi-malik, and broke his head. Gr., and crushed his skull.

div.head: Chapter IX.
div.ab:
Chapter IX. 10:1 And there arose after Abi-malik...... Tula the son of Fu a, the son of Dadheh a man from Isakhar. i.e., the son of the brother of his father, from his mother and
not from his father, since Gideon, the father of Abi-malik is from the tribe of Manasseh and not from Isakhar. 10:1 and he was living in Shamir 10:3 And there arose after him Ya ir, a Gileadite with a vowelless ain. 10:4 and he had thirty children. Gr., thirty-two. 10:5 And was buried in Gammun 10:12 And ammun has oppressed you with Revasa of Alaf. Nest. with Pethaha. 10:14 In the time of your distress. with Pethaha of Qof. 10:17 And they encamped in Mizpeh. Aq., the house of watching. 11:1 Naftah, the Gileadite, was a man of mighty valour and he was the son of a harlot. i.e., God gives heed to the hearts (character) of men and not to their lineage. 11:3 And there were gathered to Naftah vain (Lit., empty) men Gr., common(simple) men. Sim. Idle men. 11:13 From Arnon even unto Avaq.

div.head: Chapter X.
div.ab:
Chapter X. 11:24 That which Komush your God cause you to inherit. i.e., Qaramos. 11:25 And now are you better than Balak with Revasa of Mim and Zeqafa of Teth. 11:26 Why did you not recover them at that time? i.e., deliver. 11:34 And behold his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and timbrels. Gr., with dances. i.e., Naftah was not to be commanded in his vow because indiscriminately he vowed (namely) that everyone who goes out to meet me from the door of my house I shall sacrifice him as an offering. But what if a
donkey or dog came out, what would have he done? Also he was not to be blamed (
) for that he kept his covenant and honored the divine love more than the natural love. For he was not restrained as Ibrahim was as here in order that men may be restrained from unlimited vows. 11:35 O! my daughter, you have surely brought me very low. Gr., a hindrance you set up for me. Aq., you have surely made me bow low. Sim., You have surely made me kneel down. Theo., You surely restrained me. 11:40 And from time to time the daughters of Israel go and weep, and wail over the daughter of Naftah the Gileadite four days in the year. i.e., today it is not over the daughter of Naftah, but over the devastation of Jerusalem that they weep and wail. 12:5 And the people of Gilead used to ask him are you an Ephraimite, (if) he said no, then they would say to him pronounce Shavle (ears of corn, wheat) he would pronounce Savle i.e., as today the Meadites (Bedwins) pronounce the Qof like Gimmel, and the Palestinians like Alef. 12:8 Ivsan of Bethlehem 12:11 And Elun who is from Zevalon. 12:13 Akhran the son of Halyan from Afar tha. 13:2 And there was a certain man from Sidh a from the clan of Dan and his name was Manuh. 13:4 Be ware (imper. ) not to drink wine or intoxicating liquor and do not eat anything unclean. i.e., from the womb the boy Samson was made a Nazerite. 13:5 Because a Nazerite to God the boy shall be from the womb. i.e., that it might be
known that his strength was not from foods and drinks.

div.head: Chapter XI.
div.ab:
Chapter XI. 13:9 And Manuh her husband was not with her with a full pronunciation of He. 13:12 And Manuh said, shall your word come to pass presently? A question. 13:12 What shall be the customary law of the child? i.e., manner of life. 13:17 What is your name so that when your word is fulfilled we might do you honor? (Lit., call or invite) Gr., hold you in honor. 13:18 And the angel of the Lord said to him, why ask about my name which is exalted? Gr., wondrous. 13:22 And Manuh said to his wife we shall surely die because we have seen God i.e., the holy theologue says, they were in imagination of seeing God, but did not see God himself. 13:24 And called his name Samson i.e., A servant (minister). 13:25 Between Sidh a and Ishtu el 14:2 In Timnath I have seen a woman of the daughters of the Philistines, and no take her for me as a wife with a vowelless Semkath. 14:8 And he turned aside to see the skeleton of the lion Gr., the carcass. 14:12 I shall take up with you a riddle Gr., I shall propound for you an allegory. 14:12 If you interpret it for me Gr., If you make it known. 14:12 I shall give you 30 head-cloth i.e., kerchiefs or ecclesiastical head-cloth. Gr., Linen wraps. This singular is with Revasa of Kaf. 14:15 entice thy husband with a vowelless Dalath. Gr., lead astray. 14:17
Because she distressed him Gr., importuned him. 14:18 before he entered the banquet Gr., before the sunset. 14:18 What is sweeter than honey or mightier than the lion? with Zeqafa of Mim and Pethaha of Nun. 14:18 if you had not coaxed my heifer you would not have interpreted my riddle.

div.head: Chapter XII.
Chapter XIII.
div.ab:
Chapter XIII. 16:19 And she made him sleep upon her knees and called the barber Gr., the barber. 16:19 and he shaved seven locks of his head Gr., seven braids. 16:21 And the Philistines took him and blind his eyes. Gr., they bound. 16:23 They were gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their God with rejoicing with Rukkakha of Daleth. 16:30 And Samson said let my soul die with the Philistines i.e., not because he was worthy before God, that God answered his request, but that the Philistines might know that it was not by the might of Dagon they seized him, but God
delivered him because of his wantonness. 17:1 And his name was Mika 17:2 And he said to his mother the one thousand and one hundred pieces of silver which were taken on your part. i.e., stolen from you. 17:2 and you swore with Hevasa of Mim Nest. with Pethaha. Gr., and you caused to swear 17:2 that silver I took it. 17:4 And his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to the silversmith. Gr., to a founder. 17:4 and made an image engraved and molten. i.e., she had made a vow if her silver was found she will cast of it an image. 17:6 In those days there was no king in Israel. Every man did that which was beautiful in his eyes. i.e., by this word he repeatedly puts the concluding seal on this book so as to affirm that without kingdom the law would not be observed. 17:7 And there was a certain young man from Bethlehem of Judah whose name was Lawi, i.e., from the tribe of Lawi. His name then is Yunathan the son of Manassah the son of Girshan, the son of Moses the great as the chapter after this shows. And St. Jacob of Edessa says, this one, since he envied the children of Aaron desired the priesthood iniquitously and went out wandering hither and thither, and when he arrived at the house of Mika he received him and clothed him with an Ephod and a priestly garment and made him a priest for his idol. 18:1 And in those days the tribe of Dan was seeking for himself a portion (of land) to dwell in, for
until that day the inheritance was not divided among the tribes of Israel. i.e., this word is not right in the Syriac in that Joshua the son of Nun had already divided the land long ago. (
) And the seventh lot had come forth to the sons of Dan, Sidh a, and Ishtu el, etc. But because the tribe of Dan was not satisfied with the piece of land, he sought another portion. 18:9 Nor should you be slothful to go Gr., you should not tarry.

div.head: Chapter XIV.
div.ab: Chapter XIV. 18:17 And they took the image, the Ephod, the priestly garment, and the graven image. with a vowelless and Revasa of Shin. 19:1 And he took for himself a concubine. i.e., the false priest Yunathan. 19:2 And his concubine committed adultery against him. Gr., his concubine became angry at him. 19:3 And her husband got up and went after her to fill (satisfy) her heart, and bring her back. Gr., to reconcile. 19:5 Sustain your heart with a piece of bread with Pethaha of Qof 19:8 And linger about with Qushshaya of the two Kof. Gr., delay. Aq., tarry. Sim., stay around. 19:12 We shall not turn to a strange village i.e., the house of Israel had no dominance over Yahbush, which is Jerusalem, yet. 19:13 And shall spend the night in Geva or Ramath.

div.head: Chapter XV.
div.ab:
Chapter XV. 19:22 And behold the people of the village were wicked men, and they went around the house (encompassed). i.e., the children of Benjamin. They were almost like the Sadomites in respect to the women of Abraham. 19:24 Behold here
is my virgin daughter and her concubine. i.e., this old man, the host, resembled Lot. 19:25 nd they had sexual intercourse with her and abused her all night. Gr., They amused themselves with her. Aq., They were licentious with her. Theod., And they took turns with her. 19:26 Until it was dawn i.e., until it was day. Gr., until she was entirely still. 19:29 And he cut her concubine into 12 pieces. Gr., he dismembered her. 20:16 Every one who throws with the sling at the whirlwind and misses not. i.e., something flying in the air and would not miss. Gr., slingers who throw stones at a hair and do not miss. 20:25 And again the children of Benjamin destroyed from Israel 18000 men on the earth. i.e., In the two times 40,000. And because their zeal was not from God, God turned away from them in the beginning. For at Mika who casted an idol they were not angry, but because of a wife of a man who was corrupt they were kindled with zeal. 20:28 And Finhas the son of Ali azar the son of Aaron the priest was standing before him in that day. i.e., some people say that this man was not the first Finhas, but his grandson. 20:31 And they were withdrawn from the village. i.e., they went far. Gr., They were led away.

div.head: Chapter XVI.

div.ab: The Book of Judges, which is called Shavte, finished.
